chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi Umayr from Abu Ayyub from Abu Basir said:

Abd al-Hamid asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) while I was with him about the Qunut on Friday, and he said: 'In the second rak'ah.' He said to him: 'Some of our companions have narrated to us that you said in the first rak'ah.' He said: 'In the last one.' And there were many people with him, so when he saw their confusion, he said: 'O Abu Muhammad, it is in the first and the last [rak'ah].' I said: 'May I be your ransom, is it before the bowing or after it?' He said: 'All Qunut is before the bowing, except for Friday, for in the first rak'ah the Qunut is before the bowing, and in the last one it is after the bowing.'
ai.seo_question: When should the Qunut be recited during Friday prayer according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the jurisprudential nuance in Imam al-Sadiq’s (AS) practice, where he initially corrected a companion regarding the timing of Qunut in the Friday prayer before clarifying the comprehensive ruling for the congregation. It establishes the distinct procedural difference between the first rak'ah (Qunut before Ruku') and the second (Qunut after Ruku'), reflecting the scholarly tradition of adapting rulings to the understanding of the listeners. This detail is crucial for Shia fiqh regarding the completeness of the Friday prayer structure.
